record_reviews.summary: Gray’s June 21 note gives firsthand observations: pollen is already on stigmas in Dicentra, Adlumia and Corydalis before insects can enter, leading him to conclude Fumariaceae are arranged for self-fertilization. Its source apparatus marks CD’s later notes separately. It cannot answer Darwin’s July 4 letter because it predates it; Darwin says the May 21 note is still unanswered and a June 21 letter had not yet arrived.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin’s November 18 request seeks published or observed evidence on whether dark-complexioned, black-haired Europeans are more or less liable to yellow fever than light-complexioned Europeans. He notes uncertainty about having asked similar questions before and mentions his Gardeners’ Chronicle notice. The editorial apparatus identifies Gray’s later forwarding to Engelmann, but no reply or incoming evidence is preserved here.

record_reviews.summary: Darwin sends Gray the Origin abstract and requests a complete straight-through reading plus an assessment of weakest and best parts. This is a request and forecast of future reading, not evidence that Gray’s book had yet been read by Darwin or that a Gray prompt survives.
